newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's OK for Shell JV refinery seen soon.
newsitem.headline: China's OK for Shell JV refinery seen soon.

text.p: Beijing is expected to give its approval to Royal/Dutch Shell's multi-billion dollar joint venture refinery project in southern China before end-1996, Chinese oil officials said on Monday.
"From what I know, it will be approved very soon by the Chinese government," a senior Chinese oil official said by telephone from Beijing.
"It will probably be this year," said the official, who declined to be named.
The US$6 billion refinery and chemical complex, planned for Huizhou in southern China's booming Guangdong province, has been on the drawing board since the late 1980s.

Shell holds 50 percent of the complex and China National Offshore Oil Corp (CNOOC) 20 percent, while the Guangdong provincial government, state-owned shipping firm China Merchants Holding Company and state refiner Sinopec each have 10 percent.
"The Chinese side and Shell have discussed this for several years. Both sides have spent a lot of effort, money," the official said.
China, too, realised it needed to raise its production of oil and petrochemical products to meet increasing oil demand in coming years, he said.
The project, for which a feasibility study was completed in February 1994, has been facing hurdle after hurdle since the early 1990s, from high costs to strained Sino-British relations.
"This project was initially thought to be gunned down...because it was too costly. But now, they want to go ahead with it," a source with state refiner Sinopec said by telephone.
It faced its latest headache when a Shell employee and a CNOOC worker were detained in March for what a senior CNOOC earlier said was leakage of state secrets to the Shell employee.
A Shell spokesman said the company was hopeful of a decision on the joint venture project from Beijing soon.
"We note a genuine, positive feeling among everybody concerned," the spokesman said.
